items.title: British Pound futures bounce as UK consumer confidence hits 2-year high.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures rebounded to close out the week following improved UK consumer confidence and hawkish signals from the Bank of England. After finishing higher in just two of the previous 11 sessions, the pound saw a lift as short covering emerged ahead of the weekend. Support also materialized as UK consumer confidence unexpectedly jumped to a two-year high, with GfK's index rising to minus 13 for September. Market expectations shifted as Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden and Governor Andrew Bailey highlighted inflation risks, noting that elevated energy costs could make it increasingly difficult to hold rates steady and leaving further rate hikes on the table.

items.title: Crude's supply risks meet a 66.4% probability of a Fed hike.
items.excerpt: The week of Sept. 28 brings a critical slate of economic data, central bank developments, and energy market catalysts. Traders will monitor Strait of Hormuz discussions and an upcoming OPEC+ meeting for immediate impacts on WTI Crude Oil futures. Attention also shifts to the U.S., where July PCE and August Nonfarm Payrolls will provide the latest view on inflation and hiring ahead of the October FOMC meeting. The CME FedWatch Tool currently reflects a 66.4% probability of another rate hike. Alongside a busy macroeconomic calendar featuring PMIs and inflation figures from across the globe, the earnings schedule offers updates from 18 large-cap companies, including Micron Technology and Nike.

items.title: Commodity weekly: Macro pressure meets supply tightness
items.excerpt: Key Points: Macro headwinds intensified , with surging US bond yields and a stronger dollar putting pressure on commodities, particularly precious metals. Physical tightness remains a powerful counterweight , helping industrial metals, energy and selected agricultural markets resist the broader macro pressure. Oil remains caught between improving flows and persistent disruption , as diplomacy, renewed attacks and costly workarounds keep the physical market far from normal. Copper and soybean meal highlight the supply story , with low inventories, strong demand and weather-related disruption supporting prices despite an increasingly challenging macro backdrop. items.title: Has the era of cheap food come to an end?
items.excerpt: From climate shocks, including the effects of El Niño, and rising labour costs to changing welfare standards and technological innovation, food prices may be entering a new structural regime. In this episode, Heidi Richardson and Sreedhar Mahamkali from UBS Research discuss the forces driving this shift, the potential role of technology as a counterbalance, and what a structurally higher food inflation environment could mean for consumers, businesses and markets. *(This information is subject to a disclaimer at the end of this podcast. Please ensure that you listen to the disclaimer and go to www.ubs.com for further information about UBS).

items.excerpt: Dan Deming outlines the recent price action across major FX markets, noting that Australian Dollar futures have traded lower for a third consecutive session to reach two-month lows near the 0.7020 level. items.excerpt: Bitcoin has recovered roughly 37% since mid-August, and IBIT’s options market is pricing calmer conditions than the last five weeks actually delivered. items.title: Euro futures drop to 8-week lows amid hawkish Fed speak.
items.excerpt: Euro futures fell to an eight-week low of 1.1409, marking their seventh lower close in the past 10 sessions. Despite Eurozone manufacturing PMI data coming in slightly stronger than expected at 52.7, the euro continued its slide. Germany's PMI missed forecasts, dropping to 53.8, though both regions remain in expansion territory. Meanwhile, the U.S. dollar moved to multi-week highs following hawkish comments from Fed Governor Michael Barr, who signaled further rate hikes are likely needed. According to CME Group's FedWatch Tool, the probability of an October rate hike climbed to over 70%. U.S. composite PMI also reached its highest level since July 2021, reinforcing market expectations and adding further pressure to the euro as Treasury yields increased.

Global yields are climbing across the board, with the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield hitting its highest level since early 2025 and the probability of a September FOMC rate hike rising. Looking ahead, focus shifts to the Fed's Beige Book, ongoing corporate earnings, and key rate decisions from the RBA and Bank of Canada.

items.title: Copper’s growing importance in a changing world
items.excerpt: Key Points: Copper is trading near record highs, supported by structural demand from electrification, power grids, AI and data centres, defence and reindustrialisation. Friedland s supply arithmetic highlights the scale of the challenge : the world may need to mine as much copper during the next 18 years as throughout history, even before fully accounting for electrification and AI. Declining ore grades and lengthy development timelines constrain supply , requiring more energy, water and capital while limiting how quickly higher prices can bring new production. The long-term outlook remains supportive, but near-term risks are significant , including a reversal of US stockpiling, slower AI and data-centre investment, weaker demand and elevated speculative positioning that could amplify…

items.title: US diesel export ban: A political quick fix that could make the problem worse
items.excerpt: Key Points: Political appeal, economic risk: Speculation the US administration could introduce an export ban on diesel has widened WTI's discount to Brent while driving the Brent-gasoil spread to a fresh record A US diesel export ban could temporarily boost domestic inventories and ease prices, but it would redistribute rather than solve the underlying global shortage. A ban could ultimately reduce fuel supply: Once Gulf Coast storage fills, refiners may be forced to cut throughput, reducing production of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel while removing up to 1.5 million barrels per day of diesel from an already tight global market. The Trump administration is considering restricting US diesel exports as record fuel prices intensify pressure on consumers, farmers and transport companies.…

items.title: British Pound futures slide to two-month lows on central bank divergence.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures continued their downward trajectory, trading near two-month lows after declining in six of the last seven sessions. Selling pressure persisted at 1.3330, driven by a divergence in central bank policies following the Bank of England's decision to hold rates steady while the Fed hiked. Geopolitical discussions at the United Nations also added to intraday volatility. The pullback marks a sharp reversal from a six-month high reached just four weeks ago. A similar pattern emerged in Euro futures, which also hit two-month lows as the U.S. Dollar Index climbed to a two-month high. Australian Dollar and Canadian Dollar futures experienced milder declines across a broadly softer FX complex.
